hindi: श्यामा आदि के कल्क से युक्त यह लेह सिद्ध विरेचन है।
english: This leha (a preparation to be licked), joined with a paste of śyāmā and the others, is an accomplished purgative.
notes: śyāmā is kept as a drug name (it also means 'dark'). Units in this chunk are single printed half-verse lines; a sentence often runs on into the next unit.

words.gloss: of pathyā, akṣa, the ten roots

hindi: उसी प्रकार पथ्या, अक्ष और दशमूल के लेह अलग-अलग रसों से बनाए जाते हैं।
english: Likewise the lehas of pathyā, akṣa and the daśamūla (the ten roots) are made with separate juices.
notes: No verb in the Sanskrit; 'are made' is supplied in both translations. pathyā and akṣa are kept as drug names (pathyā literally 'wholesome'). 'tadvat' is taken as 'in the same way' as the leha of the previous unit; the referent is not stated.

hindi: उन दोनों का चूर्ण, विड के बराबर, उसी के रस से ही भावित किया हुआ।
english: Of those two, a powder equal to viḍa, steeped in its own juice alone.
notes: 'tayoḥ' (of those two): the referent is not clear (perhaps pathyā and akṣa of the previous unit). 'viḍasamam' could also be 'equal quantity of viḍa'. viḍa is kept as a drug name. bhāvita = steeped, soaked through.

hindi: विबन्ध में, मल में और वात से उत्पन्न गुल्म में, खट्टे से युक्त यह हितकर है।
english: In obstruction (vibandha), in the stool, and in gulma risen from Vāta, it is beneficial when joined with something sour.

text_flags.why: possible: 'viśi' gives no clear sense here; 'viḍi' (loc. of viḍ, stool) would pair with vibandha; metre is 16 syllables either way

notes: The reading of 'viśi' is doubtful; 'in the stool' is only a guess. 'it' (the preparation of the earlier units) is supplied as subject. gulma is kept as a disease name.
lines_deva: विबंधे विशि वातोत्थे गुल्मे चाम्लयुतं हितं
lines_iast: vibaṃdhe viśi vātotthe gulme cāmlayutaṃ hitaṃ

hindi: मुद्ग आदि के साथ पकाई गई उनकी जड़ों से यूष आदि तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare soups (yūṣa) and the like with their roots, cooked with mudga and the like.
notes: Construction is loose: 'siddhaiḥ' and 'tanmūlaiḥ' are both instrumental plural; 'cooked with mudga etc.' is taken with 'their roots'. 'their' (tat) has no clear referent. mudga is kept as a name.

words.gloss: drug names: dantī, dravantī, marica, svarṇakṣīrī, yavānaka

hindi: दन्ती, द्रवन्ती, मरिच, स्वर्णक्षीरी और यवानक,
english: dantī, dravantī, marica, svarṇakṣīrī and yavānaka,
notes: All five are kept as drug names. The sentence continues in the next unit.

hindi: शुण्ठी, अग्निक और पृथ्वीक के साथ, चूर्ण किया हुआ, समान दिनों तक।
english: together with śuṇṭhī, agnika and pṛthvīka, powdered, for equal days.
notes: 'samavāsarān' (accusative of duration, 'for equal days') is unclear in context; perhaps linked to the steeping in the next unit. Not firmly resolved. śuṇṭhī, agnika, pṛthvīka kept as drug names.

hindi: मूत्र से भावित को घी के साथ पीए, और जीर्ण हो जाने पर तर्पण लेना चाहिए।
english: Steeped in urine, one should drink it with ghee; and when it is digested, tarpaṇa (satiation).
notes: 'tarpaṇam' has no verb; 'should be taken' supplied in Hindi. What is digested (jīrṇe) is not stated.

hindi: सदा, सभी रोगों में तथा बालक और वृद्ध में वह हितकर है।
english: Always, in all ailments and in a child and an old person, that is beneficial.
lines_deva: सर्वदा सर्वरोगेषु बाले वृद्धे च तद्धितं
lines_iast: sarvadā sarvarogeṣu bāle vṛddhe ca taddhitaṃ

words.gloss: in ill-eating, indigestion, side-pain, gulma, spleen, belly

hindi: और दुर्भुक्त, अजीर्ण, पार्श्व की पीड़ा, गुल्म, प्लीहा और उदर में।
english: and in ill-eating, indigestion, pain in the side, gulma, the spleen and the belly (udara).
notes: 'plīhodareṣu' is taken as 'spleen' and 'belly' separately; it could also be one term, 'plīhodara'.

hindi: गण्डमाला में, वात में और पाण्डुरोग में वह प्रशंसित है।
english: In gaṇḍamālā (a named ailment, literally 'garland of lumps'), in Vāta, and in pāṇḍu-roga (the pale-ailment), it is commended.

text_flags.why: b/v confusion common in this edition; 'vāta' is the term meant (Vāta)

lines_deva: गंडमालासु बाते च पांडुरोगे च शस्यते
lines_iast: gaṃḍamālāsu bāte ca pāṃḍuroge ca śasyate

hindi: आठ पल गुड़ के साथ बीस पथ्या हों, एक-एक पल।
english: To eight palas of jaggery (guḍa), there should be twenty pathyā, a pala each.
notes: 'palaṃ palaṃ' is repeated for distribution ('a pala each'); it may instead refer to the drugs of the next unit, or to the weight of the pathyā. Quantities unclear. pala is a measure of weight.

hindi: दन्ती और चित्रक के दो कर्ष, पिप्पली और त्रिवृत् के दस।
english: Of dantī and citraka, two karṣas; of pippalī and trivṛt, ten.
notes: karṣa is a measure. The unit of 'ten' is not stated (presumably karṣas). It is unclear whether 'two karṣas' is for each or both. dantī, citraka, pippalī kept as drug names; trivṛt is literally 'threefold', kept as a drug name.

hindi: मोदक बनाकर, प्रत्येक दसवें दिन एक।
english: Having prepared the balls (modaka), one on every tenth day,
notes: 'ekam' is taken as 'one' (one ball at a time); the verb comes in the next unit.

hindi: ऊपर से गरम जल पीते हुए, इस विधि से उन सबको खाए।
english: drinking warm water after, one should eat all of them by this method.

hindi: ये परिहार से रहित हों, सब व्याधियों के नाशक।
english: These would be without avoidances (restrictions), destroyers of all ailments.
notes: niṣparihāra: literally 'without avoidance', taken as having nothing to be avoided.

words.gloss: of grahaṇī, pāṇḍu, itch, koṭha, arśas

hindi: विशेष रूप से ग्रहणी, पाण्डु, कण्डु, कोठ और अर्श के लिए ये हितकर हैं।
english: Especially, they are beneficial for grahaṇī, pāṇḍu, itching (kaṇḍu), koṭha and arśas.
notes: grahaṇī, koṭha, arśas are kept as the names given. The genitive 'of' is rendered 'for'.

hindi: विरेचन में ये त्रिवृत् आदि ही सबसे मुख्य नहीं हैं।
english: In purging, these trivṛt and the rest are not indeed the most principal.
notes: 'naivaite' = na eva ete; the sense (not the chief ones, or not the only ones) is unclear. Rendered literally; the next unit adds harītakī. Sense check: the negation sits oddly beside the next unit, which prepares harītakī 'also' by the trivṛt method. The printed text is kept; a misprint is possible but no emendation is proposed.

hindi: हरीतकी को भी त्रिवृत् की विधि से तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare harītakī also by the method of trivṛt.

words.gloss: removing grahaṇī, pāṇḍu, wasting, bewilderment, belly

hindi: विशेषतः ग्रहणी, पाण्डु, शोष, मोह और उदर को दूर करने वाली।
english: especially removing grahaṇī, pāṇḍu, wasting (śoṣa), bewilderment (moha) and the belly (udara).
notes: 'apahām' (feminine) qualifies harītakī of the previous unit. 'udara' is rendered with its plain sense 'belly'; it could also be a named ailment.

hindi: सिन्धूत्थ, विडङ्ग, उत्पल और नागर के साथ पथ्या को पीए।
english: One should drink pathyā together with sindhūttha, viḍaṅga, utpala and nāgara.
notes: All four are kept as drug names (utpala also means lotus; nāgara literally 'of the city').

hindi: मूत्र से, अथवा वत्सक आदि के क्वाथ से, हरीतकी को।
english: With urine, or with a decoction of vatsaka and the others, harītakī.
notes: The verb (pibet, 'should drink') is carried over from the previous unit. niryūha rendered 'decoction' as in the glossary (OPEN: keep apart from kaṣāya/kvātha or not); Hindi क्वाथ.

hindi: अथवा पथ्या और नागर का चूर्ण, कोलिनी के फल से संयुक्त।
english: Or a powder of pathyā and nāgara, joined with kolinī fruit.

text_flags.why: two words run together (missing space); possibly also a faulty case ending on -phale

notes: The locative 'kolinīphale' is rendered 'with'. kolinī is kept as a drug name. Reading uncertain.

hindi: गुड़ के साथ खाए, और उसके बाद गुनगुना जल पीए।
english: One should eat it with jaggery, and drink lukewarm water afterwards.

hindi: पथ्या और त्रिवृत् से गोलियाँ बनानी चाहिए, शहद और रस से युक्त।
english: Pills should be made from pathyā and trivṛt, accompanied by honey and juice.

text_flags.why: 'ddhāṃ' is not a valid ending; dual 'bhyām' (from pathyā and trivṛt) fits sense and the 16-syllable metre

notes: 'kṣaudra' is taken as honey; 'kṣaudrarasa' could also be one term, 'honey-juice'.

hindi: माष के परिमाण की वे सूखी गोलियाँ, यक्ष्मन् से ग्रस्त घी में द्रवित करके चाटे।
english: Those dry pills, of the measure of a māṣa, one with yakṣman should lick, melted in ghee.

text_flags.why: possible: 'lihmāt' is not a form (√lih opt. is lihyāt) and 'ddhṛta' is likely a misread 'ghṛta' (melted in ghee)

notes: māṣa is a small measure. 'drutāḥ' is taken as 'melted'. yakṣman is kept as a disease name. 'dry' and 'melted in ghee' both qualify the pills as printed; how they fit together is not stated.

hindi: पथ्या, त्रिवृत्, कटु और गरम जल सर्वत्र इष्ट विरेचन है।
english: Pathyā, trivṛt, kaṭu (pungent) and hot water: a purgative desired everywhere.
notes: 'kaṭuṣṇāṃbu' could also be 'pungent hot water' or 'trikaṭu' with a lost syllable; the four-item reading is taken.

hindi: पथ्या का चूर्ण स्नुक् के क्षीर से भावित हो जाने पर मोदक बनाए।
english: When the powder of pathyā has been steeped in snuk-milk, one should make balls (modaka).
notes: snuk is kept as a drug name; kṣīra = milk.

hindi: कोल की गुठली के माप वाले और सूखे मोदकों को ताज़े मक्खन के साथ चटाए।
english: One should make (him) lick the balls, of the size of a kola seed and dry, with fresh butter.
notes: 'modakān' is carried over from the previous unit. kola is kept as a fruit name. lehayet is the causative of √lih; glossary OPEN: literal 'should make (him) lick'.

words.gloss: of one with gulma, belly, liver, spleen, pain, ānāha, obstruction

hindi: गुल्म, उदर, यकृत्, प्लीहा, शूल, आनाह और विबन्ध वाले का,
english: of one with gulma, belly (udara), liver, spleen, pain (śūla), ānāha (tying-up) and obstruction (vibandha),
notes: '-vibandhinaḥ' could be genitive singular or nominative/accusative plural; taken as 'of one with ...' with the licking of the next unit. The unit is a dependent phrase.

words.gloss: joined with kuṣṭha and the three pungents

hindi: कुष्ठ और त्रिकटुक से युक्त को एरण्ड के तैल के साथ चाटे।
english: One should lick it, joined with kuṣṭha and the trikaṭuka (the three pungents), with eraṇḍa oil.
notes: The object ('it') is not named; 'etat' of the next unit refers back. kuṣṭha and eraṇḍa are kept as drug names.

hindi: और ऊपर से सुखद जल पीए; यह विरेचन सुखकर है।
english: And one should drink pleasant water after; this purgative is easy.
notes: sukha: 'pleasant, comfortable' (possibly comfortably warm; not stated).

hindi: थोड़े का भी बड़ा प्रयोजन और अधिक का थोड़ा कर्म,
english: Great purposefulness even of a small amount, and smallness of action of a large amount,
notes: arthatva: 'purposefulness, usefulness'. Governed by 'kuryāt' in the next unit.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (member of compound continuing)

hindi: संश्लेष, विश्लेष, काल, संस्कार और युक्ति के द्वारा करे।
english: one may bring (these) about by means of combination, separation, time, processing and method (yukti).
notes: The space after 'saṃśleṣa' is read as a missing hyphen: 'saṃśleṣa-viśleṣa-kāla-saṃskāra-yuktibhiḥ'. The subject is not stated.

hindi: त्वक्, केसर, आम्रातक, दाडिम, एला, सितोपला, माक्षिक और मातुलुङ्ग के साथ,
english: with tvak (bark), kesara, āmrātaka, dāḍima, elā, sitopalā (literally 'white stone'), mākṣika and mātuluṅga,

text_flags.why: space inside 'āmrātaka': printed 'tvakkesarā mrātaka' stands for 'tvakkesarāmrātaka' (tvak-kesara-āmrātaka)

notes: All names are kept as drug names. mākṣika is literally 'of the bee' and also a substance name; left unresolved. 'tvak-kesara' may be one drug or two (bark; filament).

hindi: मद्य से और उन-उन मन के अनुकूल वस्तुओं से युक्त विरेचन देने चाहिए।
english: Purgatives should be given, mixed with madya (an intoxicating drink) and with those various things agreeable to the mind.
notes: 'things' is supplied in the translations. Continues the instrumental list of the previous unit. madya = intoxicating drink.

hindi: इस प्रकार विरेचनकल्प नामक द्वितीय अध्याय।
english: Thus the second chapter, named Virecanakalpa (the purgative preparations).
notes: GROUPING: this is the chapter colophon, not a verse; it is typed as a verse in the input but is a prose closing line.
